name: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia

criteria.description: Presence of tibial nonunion or pseudoarthrosis evident on imaging
Anterior or anterolateral bowing of the tibia noted clinically or radiographically
Nonunion occurring without history of trauma or fracture
Presence of neurofibromatosis type 1 features or NF1 gene mutation
Radiographic evidence of cystic or sclerotic changes at the site of pseudoarthrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of tibial nonunion with anterior bowing of the tibia in the absence of trauma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing for NF1 may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Definitive feature characterized by false joint formation
searchTerms: shin bone nonunion with false joint

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior or anterolateral bowing of the tibia
pathognomonic.notes: Usually present at birth or early infancy
searchTerms: shin bone bending forward or to side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fracture of the tibia with failure to heal
pathognomonic.notes: Occurs spontaneously or after minor trauma
searchTerms: tibia fracture that fails to heal
broken shin bone with delayed healing

common.symptomName: Pain localized to the affected tibia
Soft tissue swelling around the pseudoarthrosis site
common.notes: May be due to fibrous tissue proliferation
searchTerms: soft tissue swelling near tibia pseudoarthrosis

common.symptomName: Limited mobility or deformity of the lower leg
common.notes: Secondary to bone deformity and instability

occasional.notes: Present in a subset of patients
searchTerms: pigmented skin marks linked to NF1

occasional.symptomName: Muscle atrophy of the affected leg
occasional.notes: Due to disuse or nerve involvement
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in lower limb

occasional.symptomName: Joint stiffness adjacent to the pseudoarthrosis
searchTerms: limited joint movement next to pseudoarthrosis
fibula bone fractures that heal poorly

rare.notes: Due to mass effect from fibrous tissue
searchTerms: tingling or numbness from nerve pressure
long-term bone infection at false joint
chronic bone infection where bone fails to heal

laboratory: Genetic testing for NF1 mutations if neurofibromatosis suspected
imaging: X-ray showing tibial bowing and pseudoarthrosis with sclerotic bone ends
MRI to assess soft tissue and fibrous hamartoma at pseudoarthrosis site
Bone scan may show decreased uptake at pseudoarthrosis
genetic: Mutations in NF1 gene in approximately 50% of cases
No specific gene identified in isolated CPT without NF1
other: Histopathology of pseudoarthrosis site shows fibrous tissue and abnormal periosteum

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized bone fragility with multiple fractures

redFlags: Failure of tibial fracture to heal after standard treatment
Progressive deformity and bowing of the tibia in infancy
Development of pathological fractures with minimal trauma
references: Joseph B, et al. Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia: a review of current concepts. J Orthop Surg Res. 2018.
Orphanet: Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
Deng Z, et al. Management of congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia: a systematic review. Bone Joint J. 2020.
